v.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes training into divergence, as in runs 5 and 6 with drops of up to 47 points.
Lowering a very large learning rate restores stable training, as in runs 11, 13, 14 and 18 with gains of up to 68 points.
Shallower networks tolerate large learning rates better, as in runs 72 and 75 with gains of 35 to 71 points.
Strong L2 near 1 underfits, so reducing it helps, as in runs 91, 97 and 100.
Increasing an already large L2 penalty worsens underfitting, as in runs 85 and 86.
With 243 epochs, very small learning rates undertrain, so a step up helps, as in run 7 (+21 on vehicle).
Extra regularization on top of an unstable high learning rate worsens fit, as in runs 84, 87 and 90.
Deep three-layer networks are the most prone to divergence at high learning rates, so lowering the rate gains the most there, as in runs 11, 14, 18 and 75.
Narrower layers have smaller pre-activations and are more stable at large learning rates, as in run 56.
Adding layers makes high-learning-rate training less stable.

raw:
These hypotheses come from the 100 experiments and general MLP training behavior. Large learning rates cause divergence, and wider or deeper networks are more fragile there. Heavy L2 at alpha near 1 underfits. I did not run any further checks beyond the supplied measurements.
